sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submits that respondent Nos.3 to 6 remained ex-parte before the Tribunal, hence notice is not required to them in the appeal.

4.1 Appellant - petitioner has filed claim petition under Sections 140(C) and 166 of the MV Act, 1988 read with Rule 475(1)(b) of APMV Rules, 1989, claiming compensation of Rs.4,62,000/- with interest from the date of decree till the date of realization against all the respondents jointly and severally for the injuries sustained by him in the accident.

4.2 On 12.12.2004, the appellant - petitioner was proceedings on his Hero Honda Splendor motor cycle bearing No.AP-25-K-6252 from Mehdipatnam to Secunderabad along with his sister Praveena, when they reached near Dwaraka Hotel at Lakdikapul at about 11.45 a.m., one setwin bus, route No.1584/U bearing registration No.ADT-8296 came in a rash and negligent manner, dashed the motor cycle from back side.

Consequently, the appellant - petitioner and his sister fell down, he received injuries, he was taken to Global hospital and from there he was BRMR,J shifted to NIMS Hospital, where he was treated as in patient for 36 days.
Even after discharge from the Hospital he took treatment by staying in the house from a private doctor.
Appellant - petitioner was aged about 30 years as on the date of accident and was earning Rs.8,000/- per month as a lab technician.

On the complaint, Police Saifabad has registered a case in crime No.970 of 2004 under Section 338 of IPC against respondent No.3.
5.
Respondent No.1 filed counter and denied the manner in which the accident has taken place.
Respondent No.2 has also filed its counter and denied the accident.
Respondent Nos.3 to 6 remained ex parte before the Tribunal.
6. Appellant - petitioner is examined as PW1, got examined PW2 - Dr.N.Rambabu, PW3 - G.Bola Shankar, PW4 - Dr.M.Ashok Kumar and got marked Exs.A1 to A15.

Respondent No.1 has got examined RW1 - T.Venkata Ramanappa and got marked Exs.B1 and B2.
7.

The learned Tribunal after going through the evidence adduced by the parties has awarded the compensation as under:
 Sl.No.
Name of
the Head Compensation

awarded by the  Tribunal 1. Shock, pain and sufferance Rs.20,000/-
and loss of amenities for life 2. Injury Rs.30,000/-
BRMR,J 3.

Medical and incidental Rs.60,000/-
expenses G. Madhukiran vs The National Insurance Company Limited ... on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61197034/
2 4. Loss of income Rs.24,000/-

Total Rs.1,34,000/-
with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of filing the petition till the date of realization against all the respondents jointly and severally.

8. Learned counsel for the appellant - petitioner submits that the learned Tribunal failed to see that the appellant - petitioner has suffered grievous crush injury on his left foot and there is total disfiguration of the foot and that the appellant will not have normal standing and walking position for the rest of his life.
The learned Tribunal ought to have awarded full compensation as claimed by the appellant - petitioner and awarded less amount towards loss of income.

The Tribunal has totally ignored that due to permanent disability of his left leg, the appellant - petitioner cannot attend his regular activities, cannot run, cannot walk normally and will not be having a sitting job.
Counsel to substantiate his contention has relied on the decisions in the cases of (i) R.D.Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd.

Learned counsel for respondent No.1 submits that the Tribunal has rightly awarded just compensation to the appellant - petitioner and the interest awarded at the rate of 7.5% per annum has to be scaled down to 6% as per the decisions in the cases of (i) Anthony Anthony Swamy Vs.
Managing Director, Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation 4 and (ii) Benson George Vs.
Reliance General Insurance Company Limited and Another 5 .
10. Heard learned counsel and perused the material on record.
11.

sentences.text: Insofar as the loss of income is concerned, learned Tribunal has awarded Rs.24,000/- without assigning any reason.
12. It is the case of the appellant - petitioner that he is working as a lab technician and earning Rs.8,000/- per month.
The Tribunal ought to have taken the said income into consideration while arriving at loss of earning.

13. The evidence of PW2 - Dr.N.Ram Babu is that the appellant - petitioner was admitted on 12.02.2004 with crush injury on his left foot (2009) 4 SCC 513 (2011) 1 SCC 343 (2020) 7 SCC 161 (2022) 13 SCC 142 BRMR,J

with deglobing of skin with loss of little toe, he was operated on 13.12.2004 and discharged on 06.01.2005, subsequently patient was on regular follow up treatment as an out-patient, he was again readmitted on 28.01.2005 for the coverage of the residual raw areas,

he was operated on 31.01.2005, skin grafting was done and discharged on 06.02.2005, he was on a follow up treatment with orthopedic surgeon and external fixtures were removed on 23.02.2005 casing was applied and pop support was given.

sentences.text:
PW4 - Dr.M.Ashok Kumar deposed that he has attended the appellant - petitioner at his house for the purpose of dressing of his left foot having crush injury daily for a period of 70 days i.e., from 08.02.2005 to 23.04.2005, he carried out the dressing to his left foot, he charged Rs.300/- per day towards his fees and transportation charges, the appellant has paid Rs.21,000/- towards his fee, the patient was bed ridden and was not in a position to move.
15.1
In view of the evidence of PW2 and PW4 this Court feels that the appellant - petitioner has suffered loss of earning for six months as held in Raj Kumar case3.

15.2 In R.D.Hattangadi1 Supreme Court observed that when fixing an amount of compensation payable to a victim of an accident the damages BRMR,J have to be assessed separately as pecuniary damages and special damages.
16. The Tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.20,000/- towards shock, pain and suffering and loss of amenities to life, which are on lower side.
The appellant - petitioner is entitled for transportation charges, extra nourishment, cost of hospitalization, cost of dressing, which are mentioned in the calculation sheet.
The appellant - petitioner is also entitled for enhanced amount towards pain and suffering.

17. Learned counsel for the appellant - petitioner has claimed an amount of Rs.30,000/- towards continuing permanent disability, he is not entitled for the same in view of the fact that there is no material placed on record.

18. The calculation arrived by this Court is as under:
 Sl.No. Name of the Head Compensation  awarded by this  Court  1. Loss of income for six months Rs.48,000/-
 (Rs.8,000/- per month) (8,000 x 6)
 2. Injury Rs.30,000/-
 3.

Medical bills and Rs.60,000/-
 transportation charges  4. Cost of dressing Rs.21,000/-
 5. Extra nourishment Rs.10,000/-
 6. Pain and suffering Rs.50,000/-
BRMR,J 19.1
The learned Tribunal has awarded interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum.

4

entities.text: G. Madhukiran vs The National Insurance Company Limited
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 19.2 In Anthony Anthony Swamy4 Supreme Court has awarded interest at the rate of 6% per annum, which is followed in Benson George5.
19.3 In Supe Dei2 Three Judge Bench of the Supreme Court has awarded interest at the rate of 9% per annum.
Hence this Court is of the view that the appellant - petitioner is entitled for interest at the rate of 9% from the date of filing the petition till the date of realization.

20. In the result, MACMA.No.1325 of 2007 is partly allowed and the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced as under:
a) The impugned award dated 09.04.2007, passed in O.P.No.365 of 2005, stands modified.

b) The compensation awarded by the Tribunal i.e., Rs.1,34,000/- is enhanced to Rs.2,19,000/- together with costs and interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of filing the petition till payment.

c) All the respondents are hereby directed to deposit the awarded amount jointly and severally with interest and costs less the amount already paid if any within a period of 60 days from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
BRMR,J d) Appellant - petitioner is permitted to withdraw entire amount with costs and interest thereon without furnishing security.
As a sequel miscellaneous application/s pending if any shall stand closed.
No costs.
